page: UpCloud CLOUDNATIVE-12xCPU-32GB is a Cloud Native family virtual server running on the KVM hypervisor. It features 12 shared vCPUs mapped to 12 physical cores of an AMD EPYC 7542 processor with an x86_64 architecture. The CPU operates at a clock speed of 2.0 GHz and includes 16 MB of L3 cache. The system is equipped with 32.0 GB of system memory, providing 2.67 GB of RAM per core. No local storage or dedicated GPU hardware is bundled with this instance type, though it includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Performance benchmarks indicate a mixed profile. The server demonstrates strong single-core performance in Geekbench tests, but poor single-core performance in stress-ng tests, placing it in the bottom 10%. Multi-core CPU performance across stress-ng, Geekbench, and Passmark falls consistently into the average tier. Memory bandwidth tests for both small and large blocks also register average throughput, though the Passmark memory score is weak, ranking in the bottom 25%. For specialized workloads, the server delivers average performance in static web serving, Redis SET operations, and software compilation, but exhibits poor text generation speeds for medium-sized language models.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the shared CPU allocation model offers a resource-dense configuration for multi-threaded tasks without the premium of dedicated cores. However, the shared CPU architecture presents a tradeoff in performance consistency under sustained, heavy single-core loads. This server is best suited for general-purpose workloads, multi-threaded utility processing, static web serving, and lightweight database operations that do not require dedicated CPU execution or local NVMe storage.
